about: Stages and timing for the synonym-tune-up playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: review
stages.do: Review the user-created and Bloomreach-generated synonyms and what fires on the top queries, add the bad, risky, no-op, leftover test and missing-wording findings, and agree which to fix.

stages.name: fix
stages.do: Plan every chosen fix in one request, preview each create, update and switch-on, write batch by batch after its own yes (each switch-on and delete on its own), and hand Bloomreach-generated ones to the user for the dashboard.

skip_when.reason: the review found no synonym worth fixing.

stages.name: measure
stages.do: Check the busiest synonym change that alters what fires paid off on its query and variants, with the change and its live date from the hand-off file.

skip_when.reason: no change to a synonym that fires on live traffic went live, so there is nothing to measure.
the fix stage was skipped, so nothing changed.

notes.measure_after_days: Days after the fix stage finishes (the synonym changes went live) before the measure stage is due. Synonyms sync about hourly in production; change-impact-tracker needs about 14 days of data after a change for a verdict other than too early to tell.
notes.max_chosen: How many findings can be chosen at once. The fix stage plans every chosen finding in one request; discovery-synonym-fixer splits it into batches of its own size, with a separate yes for each switch-on and delete.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when an earlier stage had one of these outcomes, or with skipped: true when it was skipped).
